To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
plasma lipoprotein particles and apolipoprotein high density lipoproteins bind squalene, and inhibit squalene conversion to sterols.
plasma lipoprotein and apo HDL inhibit the conversion of squalene to sterol by rat liver microsome and cytosol.
plasma lipoprotein, especially high density lipoproteins, inhibit the conversion of squalene to cholesterol in rat liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism by which plasma lipoprotein inhibits the conversion of squalene to sterol.
the mechanism of action of HDL in the inhibition of sterol biosynthesis from squalene.
the mechanism of inhibition of hepatic sterol synthesis by plasma lipoprotein and HDL.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lipoproteins inhibit sterol formation from3H-squalenecatalyzed by rat liver microsome and cytosol by binding to3H-squalenenon-specifically.

the inhibition by plasma lipoprotein of the formation of cholesterol and other sterols in rat liver microsomal preparations is due to a competition of lipoprotein-bound squalene for the enzyme system which catalyzes the conversion of squalene to sterol.

the plasma lipoprotein-mediated inhibition of sterol synthesis from squalene is due to the specific binding of3H-labeled squalene to the plasma lipoprotein and/or to the HDL apolipoproteins, and that this binding is reversed by sterol carrier protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
plasma lipoprotein and apo HDL may play a role in the regulation of cholesterol biosynthesis in the liver.
plasma lipoprotein and apo HDL inhibit hepatic squalene conversion to sterol by binding squalene in vitro and in vivo.
plasma lipoprotein, particularly apo HDL, may play an important role in the inhibition of sterol synthesis from squalene in the rat liver.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inhibition of sterol synthesis by lipoproteins may be a mechanism by which lipoproteins regulate cholesterol metabolism.
plasma lipoprotein and apolipoprotein HDL can inhibit the conversion of3H- squalene to sterol by liver microsomes.
the binding of lipoproteins or apo HDL to squalene is a saturable process, which may be a mechanism for the inhibition of hepatic sterol synthesis by plasma lipoprotein.
